The question was simple: how much had each appraiser adjusted the renovated property's value relative to the neighborhood average for that renovation type?

The answer was not simple.

Five appraisers had consistently applied renovation adjustments fifteen percent above the neighborhood average. Three others had consistently applied adjustments ten percent below. The spread between the two groups was substantial. But when Rafferty checked each group's overall appraisal averages across all property types, the two groups were within one percent of each other.

"The renovation pattern is not a level difference," he said, sliding the scatter plot to the center of the table. "Their overall averages are the same. The only place these appraisers diverge is in how they value renovation work specifically."

The pattern held across three years and across multiple property types. Some appraisers valued recent renovations at a substantial premium; others treated the same renovations as less determinative of market value. Both groups produced identical overall appraisal averages. General calibration had not closed this gap because it could not see it.
examples.whatToDo: In appraisal quality review, segment appraiser adjustments by property modification type rather than only reviewing overall accuracy. An appraiser who is well-calibrated on average may show stable directional patterns in how they value specific features. Those patterns cannot be diagnosed or corrected through overall-average calibration alone.
examples.whyItMatters: A property with a recent renovation receives a different appraised value depending on which appraiser's renovation-specific pattern is applied, even when both appraisers produce the same overall average accuracy. That divergence affects lending decisions in ways that are not visible in any firm-level calibration metric.

examples.title: Air High, Water Low

planSpec.domain: environmental inspector permit pattern

examples.scenario:
You are reviewing the inspector calibration analysis for the third consecutive season. Each inspector's overall deficiency finding rate has been equalized to the same mean through the standard calibration program. The overall numbers look consistent.

Then you separate the finding rates by permit category.

Before: you assumed the standard calibration had addressed the inter-inspector variation. After: you can see it has addressed only the overall average. Two inspectors cite air-emission permit deficiencies at a rate twenty-two percent beyond their per-inspector baseline, with water-discharge permit deficiencies running fifteen percent below that same baseline. One inspector shows the reverse pattern. All three produce the same overall finding rate.

The pattern has been stable across three consecutive inspection seasons. It holds across facility sizes. It holds across regions within the state. The only variable that predicts the divergence is which inspector is assigned to which permit category.

"The calibration program equalized the averages," the analysis concludes. "It did not equalize the permit-category patterns, because the permit-category patterns were not measured in the calibration program."

Facilities with air-emission permits face higher deficiency rates when inspected by the two inspectors with the high-air pattern, independently of actual compliance. Facilities with water-discharge permits face lower rates from the same inspectors. The pattern is systematic, predictable, and invisible to a system that only tracks overall inspector stringency.
examples.whatToDo: When auditing inspector or assessor calibration, compute finding rates or outcome rates within each permit, case, or assessment sub-category, not just overall. Run the comparison after controlling for each inspector's overall rate. Stable divergences across at least three seasons indicate pattern noise that requires category-specific cross-training or joint inspection protocols.
examples.whyItMatters: Facilities' compliance costs and records are affected by which inspector's pattern-noise profile is applied to their permit type. That is a regulatory equity problem that cannot be diagnosed through overall calibration metrics.

questions.prompt: How does pattern noise differ from level noise in its source and in what calibration can address it?
choices: Pattern noise is random variation between judges; level noise is systematic variation. Average calibration removes pattern noise but leaves level noise intact.

Pattern noise is stable case-type-specific variation in how judges weight specific features; level noise is stable overall severity differences. Average calibration addresses level noise but leaves pattern noise intact.
Pattern noise and level noise are both stable but operate at different speeds; pattern noise appears within weeks while level noise takes years to develop.
questions.explanation: Level noise is a judge's stable tendency to be harsher or more lenient overall; equalizing average severity removes it. Pattern noise is a stable asymmetry by case type that survives that equalization, because it resides in how the judge weights specific features rather than in their overall average.

questions.prompt: When a performance manager's overall rating average has been equalized to the group mean through calibration, two years later the data shows that manager consistently rating technical contributors 0.5 points higher than operational contributors at the same performance level. Which conclusion is best supported?
choices: This is pattern noise: the variation is stable, case-type-specific, and survived overall average calibration.
This is occasion noise: the variation is temporary and will diminish as the manager gains more experience rating across job families.
This is level noise: the manager's overall average has not been properly calibrated yet, and completing the calibration will resolve the gap.
questions.explanation: The gap is stable across two years and is directionally consistent within a specific case type (job family) while the overall average is already calibrated. That combination is the defining signature of pattern noise: stable, sub-category-specific, and invisible to overall-average correction.

questions.prompt: When a research team wants to determine whether inter-inspector variation in deficiency finding rates is pattern noise or occasion noise, which analysis is most directly useful?
choices: Compare each inspector's overall finding rate across multiple seasons to determine whether it is stable over time.
Survey inspectors about which permit types they find most challenging to assess accurately.
Control for each inspector's overall finding rate, then compute within-permit-category rates and check whether directional differences persist across multiple seasons.
questions.explanation: Comparing overall rates tests for level noise stability, not pattern noise. Pattern noise is diagnosed by removing the overall level difference and checking whether category-specific divergences between inspectors are stable across time. Only the third option performs both of those steps.

questions.prompt: A sentencing commission has equalized all judges' average sentence lengths. Three judges still consistently sentence violent offenses above their own average and property offenses below, while two judges show the reverse. Why does this pattern persist after calibration?
choices: Because the calibration sessions were not long enough to produce lasting behavior change in the three judges.
Because violent and property offenses differ significantly in legal definitions, and judges are correctly applying those definitions differently.
Pattern noise operates within case-type distribution rather than overall severity level; equalizing averages does not change how each judge weights specific offense categories.
questions.explanation: Calibration targeted the overall average, which is where level noise lives. Pattern noise lives inside the distribution of cases: it is the judge's asymmetric weighting of offense categories. Those two things are independent, so removing one leaves the other completely intact.

questions.prompt: A radiology department finds that one radiologist has an overall finding rate identical to peers but consistently flags eighteen percent more incidental findings on chest CT scans and twelve percent fewer on abdominal MRI. What does this pattern most likely indicate?
choices: The variation is likely occasion noise because the radiologist's overall finding rate is well-calibrated and only specific scan types show the divergence.

The variation is likely pattern noise because it is stable, scan-type-specific, and survives overall-rate calibration, indicating a modality-specific calibration difference rather than a general accuracy problem.
The variation is likely level noise because it is large in magnitude; a difference of eighteen percent is too substantial to be explained by random variation.
questions.explanation: Occasion noise would not produce stable directional differences by scan type across multiple quarters. Level noise would show up in the overall finding rate, which is identical to peers. The stable, modality-specific divergence that survives overall-rate calibration is the defining signature of pattern noise.

questions.prompt: An appraisal firm conducts a calibration session that successfully equalizes all appraisers' overall averages to within one percent of each other. Which situation would indicate that pattern noise remains after calibration?
choices: Appraisers continue to show stable differences in renovation-value adjustments that are directionally consistent across multiple property types and years.
Appraisers' overall averages drift back apart within one year of the calibration session.
Appraisers disagree on specific property valuations immediately after the calibration session, before having time to apply the new standards.
questions.explanation: If overall averages drift apart, that is a level noise recurrence. If specific valuations disagree immediately post-session, that could be occasion noise or a transition effect. Only stable, directionally consistent divergence within a specific feature category across multiple periods indicates pattern noise surviving overall calibration.

questions.prompt: A school district has calibrated teacher grading averages to align with district standards. A curriculum director suspects pattern noise remains. What is the most informative next step?
choices: Conduct another calibration session with a more experienced facilitator to improve overall consistency.
Separate each teacher's grades by assessment format, remove overall average, and check whether format-specific differences are stable across cohorts.
Compare each teacher's average grade on a representative sample of student work to verify the calibration held.
questions.explanation: Running another overall calibration session cannot surface pattern noise because it measures overall averages, which have already been addressed. Comparing averages on a sample repeats the overall-level comparison. The sub-category analysis with overall-average removal is the only step that makes pattern noise visible.

questions.prompt: Which feature of judge variation is the most reliable indicator that a pattern reflects noise rather than legitimate case-specific judgment?
choices: The pattern is stable across years and across the specific facts in each case category, so it cannot be explained by case differences themselves.
The pattern is larger in magnitude than what would be expected from random variation, exceeding two standard deviations from the group mean.
The pattern is independently observed by other judges who review the same rater's decisions.
questions.explanation: Magnitude alone does not distinguish legitimate expertise differences from noise. Third-party observation can be unreliable and is not definitional. Stability across both time and within-category case facts is the key diagnostic: if the pattern holds when case-level differences within the category are controlled, the variation is coming from the judge, not the cases.

questions.prompt: A teacher shows different grading averages for essays versus quantitative work, but the gap is inconsistent across cohorts: in some semesters the teacher grades essays higher, in others lower. A district analyst concludes this is pattern noise. Is this conclusion well-supported?
choices: Yes, because any difference in grading averages by assessment type constitutes pattern noise regardless of consistency.
Yes, because two or more semesters of data are sufficient to establish a stable pattern regardless of directional consistency.

No, because pattern noise requires stability across occasions. Inconsistent directional variation across cohorts fits occasion noise better than the stable case-type-specific pattern that defines pattern noise.
questions.explanation: The defining property of pattern noise is stability: the same directional asymmetry by case type persists across different occasions and populations. A gap that reverses direction across cohorts lacks that stability and is better described as occasion noise. Pattern noise and occasion noise both vary by case, but only pattern noise varies in a consistent direction.

reviewCards.front: What is pattern noise and what makes it distinct from level noise?
reviewCards.back: Pattern noise is stable case-type-specific variation in how a judge weights specific features relative to peers, persisting even after overall average differences are removed. Level noise is the stable general tendency to be harsher or more lenient overall; equalizing averages removes level noise but leaves pattern noise intact.

reviewCards.front: Why does equalizing judges' average severity fail to address pattern noise?
reviewCards.back: Pattern noise operates within the case-type distribution, not in the overall average. A judge who weights violent crimes more heavily than property crimes will maintain that pattern after calibration because the calibration equalized the mean without asking about case-type weighting.

reviewCards.front: What analytic step distinguishes pattern noise from occasion noise?
reviewCards.back: Pattern noise is stable across occasions, seasons, and different case populations within the same type. Occasion noise is inconsistent over time. The diagnostic is to check whether the directional difference by case type holds across multiple time periods with comparable case mixes.

reviewCards.front: What intervention addresses pattern noise but not level noise?
reviewCards.back: Case-type-specific review: sorting decisions by sub-category, computing each judge's average within each type after controlling for overall level differences, and identifying stable divergences that require category-specific recalibration or cross-training.

reviewCards.front: Can a judge be perfectly calibrated on average and still produce systematic inequity?
reviewCards.back: Yes. A judge whose overall average matches peers exactly can still consistently assign outcomes above the peer average for one case type and below it for another. That asymmetry affects real cases in predictable ways and is invisible to overall-average monitoring.

implementationPlan.coreSkill: Diagnosing and correcting stable case-type-specific variation in your own or others' judgments, even after overall average calibration

ifThenPlans.context: When running a calibration program for judges, managers, or assessors and you want to verify that variation has been fully addressed
ifThenPlans.plan: After equalizing overall averages, run a secondary analysis that sorts outcomes by case sub-category and checks for stable directional differences across multiple time periods. A calibration that equalized the mean may have left pattern noise untouched.

ifThenPlans.context: When two colleagues with the same overall average still disagree systematically on specific case types
ifThenPlans.plan: Compute each colleague's average outcome within each case type and check whether the directional difference is stable across at least three periods. If it is, treat it as pattern noise rather than random variation and look for category-specific calibration rather than overall recalibration.

ifThenPlans.context: When a calibration program has been run and inter-rater disagreement persists on specific case types
ifThenPlans.plan: Separate the post-calibration data by sub-category before concluding the calibration failed. The overall average may be well-calibrated while a case-type pattern remains unaddressed. The problem is not the calibration session; it is that the calibration session measured the wrong thing.

implementationPlan.twentyFourHourChallenge: Identify one recurring judgment you make regularly. Sort your last 20 decisions by case type or sub-category. Calculate your average outcome per type. Compare those averages with a colleague's. If your overall averages are similar but your type-specific averages diverge in opposite directions, you have a candidate for pattern noise.
implementationPlan.weeklyPractice: Once a week, review one category of decisions from the past month and compare your average outcome in that category against a peer's, after removing each person's overall average. Note whether any category shows a directional difference that has appeared in the same direction for at least two consecutive months.

chapters.title: The Sources of Noise
chapters.hook: The calibration fixed level noise. Pattern and occasion noise were still running. Two-thirds of the problem was untouched.
chapters.counterintuition: Finding the dominant noise source in a judgment system does not resolve the others. Level, pattern, and occasion noise operate independently: eliminating one leaves the other two at full strength. A calibration program that equalizes overall averages addresses the level component only. If pattern noise is the larger source, that program spent its budget on the smaller problem.
chapters.tryThisNow: For a recurring judgment disagreement: note whether it is always the same person regardless of case type (level), always the same case sub-type (pattern), or the same person at different times on equivalent cases (occasion). Each yes is a separate noise source requiring its own fix.
chapters.keyTakeaway: The three noise sources operate simultaneously and independently. Addressing one without measuring the others produces incomplete improvement and leaves the dominant source potentially untouched.

breakdown.fastRead:
The investment committee's calibration program reduced inter-analyst spread by eighteen percent. At the post-program review, the chair ran a source decomposition. Level noise had accounted for thirty-three percent of total variance. The calibration had addressed one-third of the problem.

Level, pattern, and occasion noise each operate independently. Calibrating overall averages removes level noise. Structuring when assessments are committed removes occasion noise. Defining case-type criteria removes pattern noise. None of these remedies affects the other two components.

The organization that fixes only level noise still operates with sixty-seven percent of its original spread intact.
breakdown.deepRead:
An asylum assessor calibrated to the same overall approval rate as peers still brings two other sources of disagreement to every case. That is the central diagnostic fact about multi-source noise: level calibration addresses one layer and leaves the others unchanged. Knowing which layer the calibration reached is not the same as knowing which layers still need work.

Two assessors who review the same asylum claim and produce different determinations may be separated by any of the three sources, or by all of them simultaneously. If one assessor consistently approves at a higher rate regardless of case type, that is level noise. If they agree on overall approval rates but diverge on claims involving persecution type versus documentation completeness, that is pattern noise. If the same assessor reaches a different determination on the same claim seen two months later, that is occasion noise. A training program that teaches assessors to calibrate their approval rates will reduce the level component and leave the pattern and occasion components completely unaffected. If the audit shows level noise at twenty-eight percent of total spread and pattern noise at forty-five percent, a successful level calibration will leave sixty-six percent of the original spread running.

There is no single-ingredient noise problem. A judge who is level-calibrated to the same average as peers still brings their pattern noise: their private weighting of specific case features. That same calibrated judge still brings their occasion noise: the variation in their own judgments across days. Each source is a separate layer. Addressing all three is not redundancy. It is the complete work.

After correctly naming all three noise sources in its judgment system, an organization has a diagnostic map. It has not yet done the work.
breakdown.fullRead:
The refugee agency's quality director had run calibration sessions for three years before commissioning a source decomposition. The training had equalized assessors' overall approval rates across offices, and by that metric it had worked. But the matched-case audit told a different story.

The decomposition divided the total inter-assessor spread into three components. Level noise, the stable tendency of some assessors to approve at higher rates across all case types, accounted for twenty-eight percent of variance. Pattern noise, stable assessor-level differences in how persecution type versus documentation completeness was weighted, accounted for forty-five percent. Occasion noise, within-assessor variation on the same claim seen two months apart, accounted for the remaining twenty-seven percent. The three-year calibration program had addressed twenty-eight percent of the problem.

In your organization, has anyone ever measured all three noise sources simultaneously? If the answer is no, then every intervention decision has been made without a map. You know the total spread because you see the disagreement in case reviews and debriefs. But knowing the total does not tell you which tool to reach for. Pattern noise and occasion noise require entirely different remedies from each other and from level noise. Treating one as a proxy for the others is like prescribing a drug without knowing which of three conditions is causing the symptoms.

The asylum agency's calibration program had been designed to address level noise. That is a real problem, and the program solved it. But the multi-year investment had left forty-five percent of the total spread running, because pattern noise, the dominant component, had never been measured and had no intervention aimed at it. The calibration was not inadequate as a tool; it was aimed at the wrong target.

Each noise source has its own natural lever. Level noise responds to overall average equalization across assessors. Occasion noise responds to structural changes: when assessments are committed relative to when information arrives, how much information is shared before commitment, how decision sequences are organized. Pattern noise responds to case-type-specific criteria: defining more precisely what the agreed standard looks like for each major case sub-category, so that assessors stop applying private weightings to dimensions the official framework leaves underspecified.

Three sources do not require three simultaneous interventions. They require measurement first. An organization that knows its dominant source is pattern noise should target case-type criteria before investing in assessor-level calibration. An organization that finds occasion noise dominant should restructure decision timing before running calibration sessions. The intervention that matches the measurement is the one that produces the largest reduction in spread per unit of effort. The intervention that does not match the measurement produces a smaller reduction and leaves the dominant source intact.

memorableLines.text: The organization that fixes only level noise still operates with sixty-seven percent of its original spread intact.
memorableLines.why: Converts an abstract claim about noise source independence into a concrete accounting of what any single-target intervention leaves running — the number makes the oversight visible.

memorableLines.text: There is no single-ingredient noise problem. A judge who is level-calibrated to the same average as peers still brings their pattern noise: their private weighting of specific case features. That same calibrated judge still brings their occasion noise: the variation in their own judgments across days. Each source is a separate layer. Addressing all three is not redundancy. It is the complete work.
memorableLines.why: The sharpest possible statement that noise source independence is not a theoretical nuance but an operational fact: calibration produces a calibrated judge, not a consistent one.

memorableLines.text: The intervention that matches the measurement is the one that produces the largest reduction in spread per unit of effort. The intervention that does not match the measurement produces a smaller reduction and leaves the dominant source intact.
memorableLines.why: Frames source decomposition as a prerequisite for prioritization, not a theoretical exercise: without it, intervention choices are arbitrary and their cost-benefit ratio is unknowable.

examples.title: Three Sectors, One Spread

planSpec.domain: investment committee portfolio thesis review

examples.scenario:
The noise audit printout ran seven pages. Cressida had asked the analytics team to decompose eighteen months of investment thesis assessments by source component, and the pages were divided into three sections: one for level noise, one for pattern noise, one for occasion noise.

She read them in reverse order.

Occasion noise first: the same analyst rating the same thesis deck six weeks apart showed an average variation of 0.3 points. That component accounted for twenty-six percent of total inter-analyst spread. Manageable, but not small.

Pattern noise second: after removing each analyst's overall average severity, a stable directional pattern emerged. Some analysts rated early-stage technology theses more favorably than late-stage consumer theses. Others showed the opposite preference. This component accounted for forty-one percent of total variance.

Level noise last: two senior analysts consistently rated thesis strength 0.5 points above the firm average across all deal types. That component accounted for thirty-three percent.

"The calibration sessions we've been running address level noise," Cressida said, setting the pages down. "We've been solving thirty-three percent of the problem. Pattern and occasion noise have been running untouched for three years."

No single source was small enough to ignore. No single intervention addressed more than one of them.
examples.whatToDo: Before designing any noise reduction intervention for a judgment system, commission a source decomposition that separately estimates the level, pattern, and occasion components. Use the largest component to prioritize which intervention to deploy first. Report the decomposition alongside the intervention design so that the gap between what the intervention addresses and what remains is explicit from the start.
examples.whyItMatters: Capital allocation decisions in the committee depended on which analyst's noise profile dominated on a given day. Without a source decomposition, three years of calibration had produced a well-calibrated committee that still disagreed substantially on specific deal types at specific times.

examples.title: The Smallest Calibration

planSpec.domain: immigration asylum claim assessment

examples.scenario:
"The training program is working," Winsome said. "Approval rates across offices are within four percentage points of each other. Three years ago the spread was twenty-two points."

Bartholomew turned to page three of the audit. "The training is addressing level noise. Look at what it didn't address."

The matched-case audit had decomposed inter-assessor spread from 200 cases where two assessors had independently reviewed identical files. Level noise, stable differences in overall approval tendency, accounted for twenty-eight percent of total spread. Pattern noise, stable assessor-level differences in how persecution type and documentation completeness were weighted relative to each other, accounted for forty-five percent. Occasion noise, within-assessor variation on the same case reviewed two months apart, accounted for twenty-seven percent.

"So the training fixed twenty-eight percent of the problem," Winsome said.

"And left forty-five percent running," Bartholomew said. "The pattern component is the dominant source. If assessors disagree on how to weight persecution type relative to documentation, calibrating their overall approval rates doesn't help. They need guidance on what a strong documentation record looks like versus a compelling persecution narrative; not on what their overall average should be."

The training had been carefully designed and correctly implemented. It had been aimed at the wrong source.
examples.whatToDo: When evaluating a calibration program's effectiveness, measure the decomposed components before and after, not just overall spread. A program that reduces total spread by thirty percent may have addressed the level component entirely while leaving pattern and occasion components unchanged. Reporting only total spread obscures whether the intervention matched the dominant source.
examples.whyItMatters: Applicants whose claims fall into the pattern-noise-sensitive zone, cases where assessors weight persecution type and documentation differently, received different determinations based on which assessor's private weighting applied. That source of inequity was untouched by the level calibration and invisible to any metric that only tracked overall approval rates.

examples.title: Speed Versus Football IQ

planSpec.domain: sports talent scouting evaluation

examples.scenario:
Drummond posed the question to his analytics team before the decomposition results came in: how much of the inter-scout spread in prospect ratings was about scouts being generally generous or conservative, and how much was about scouts valuing different things?

The answer from three drafts of data: mostly the second.

Level noise, the stable tendency of some scouts to rate all prospects more conservatively than peers, accounted for twenty-two percent of total inter-scout variance. Pattern noise, stable scout-level differences in how speed, strength, and football IQ were weighted against each other for prospects with mixed skill profiles, accounted for fifty-two percent. Occasion noise, within-scout variation on the same film package reviewed six weeks apart, accounted for twenty-six percent.

The dominant source was not about scouts being easy or hard in general. It was about scouts having different mental models for how to weight competing dimensions. When a prospect was elite at one dimension and below average at another, scouts who prioritized speed produced a very different rating than scouts who prioritized football IQ. Both groups were internally consistent. Neither was systematically wrong. But their dimensional weighting preferences accounted for more than half of all inter-scout spread.

"Calibrating scouts to the same overall average," Drummond noted, "would address twenty-two percent of this. The biggest opportunity is getting scouts to agree on how they weight the dimensions against each other."
examples.whatToDo: When inter-rater spread in a judgment system is dominated by pattern noise, the intervention target is criteria definition rather than overall average calibration. Identify the specific case sub-types or dimensional combinations where disagreement concentrates and design the calibration around those, not around average severity.
examples.whyItMatters: Draft selection decisions for mixed-profile prospects depended on which scout's dimensional weighting appeared in the room. That is not random variation and will not average out across a draft class.

examples.title: Trace Evidence, Biological Evidence

planSpec.domain: forensic evidence evaluation

examples.scenario:
Osbourne had initiated the two-year blind re-evaluation study after noticing that the laboratory's proficiency testing program produced consistent scores but did not account for why different examiners reached different significance ratings on the same physical evidence. The proficiency program tested accuracy on known-answer cases. It did not measure what happened when examiners rated ambiguous evidence independently.

The source decomposition from the blind re-evaluation told a more complete story.

Level noise, stable tendencies of two examiners to rate all evidence types more conservatively than peers, accounted for thirty-one percent of total inter-examiner spread. Pattern noise, stable examiner-level differences in confidence when interpreting trace evidence like fiber and glass compared to fingerprint and DNA evidence, accounted for forty-three percent. Occasion noise, the same examiner's rating of the same evidence sample reviewed three months apart, accounted for twenty-six percent.

The pattern component's driver was examiner confidence in trace evidence interpretation. Some examiners applied high significance ratings to fiber evidence; others applied moderate ratings to the same sample and reserved high ratings for DNA evidence. Both groups produced the same average significance across evidence types. The divergence was trace versus biological, specifically.

"The proficiency program measures whether examiners can identify known-answer patterns," Osbourne noted in the post-study review. "That is a different question from whether examiners apply the same significance standards to the same types of ambiguous evidence. We have been measuring skill. We have not been measuring calibration to evidence type."
examples.whatToDo: Proficiency testing and noise source decomposition answer different questions. Proficiency testing tells you whether examiners can identify correct answers on known-answer cases. Source decomposition tells you whether they apply consistent criteria on ambiguous cases. Both are needed; neither substitutes for the other.
examples.whyItMatters: Case disposition depended on which examiner's pattern toward trace evidence applied. A significance rating from a trace-evidence-generous examiner and one from a trace-evidence-conservative examiner produced different forensic report conclusions for the same physical sample.

examples.title: Foreign Contact Weight

planSpec.domain: military security clearance adjudication

examples.scenario:
The hearing room was quiet and fluorescent, the kind of lighting that flattened everything into the same gray bureaucratic tone. Millard spread the adjudication noise audit across the table and let the review board read for two minutes before speaking.

The total inter-adjudicator spread decomposed into three components. Level noise, some adjudicators approving applicants at a systematically lower rate across all case types, accounted for twenty-nine percent of variance. Pattern noise, adjudicator-level divergence in how foreign contact cases were assessed specifically, accounted for forty-eight percent. Occasion noise, within-adjudicator re-classification of the same case six months later, accounted for twenty-three percent.

The pattern component's driver was explicit in the data: adjudicators disagreed most on cases involving a single foreign-national contact. Some treated a single documented contact as elevated risk; others required a pattern of contacts before applying the same risk weight. Both groups produced the same overall approval rates. The divergence was foreign-contact cases specifically.

"Our calibration program addresses overall approval rates," Millard said. "That is the twenty-nine percent. The largest component, forty-eight percent, is about how adjudicators define what a meaningful foreign contact is. That is the question we have never put on the calibration agenda."

The board's existing training had produced adjudicators who agreed on their averages and disagreed, substantially, on the case type that generated nearly half of all inter-adjudicator spread.
examples.whatToDo: When a noise audit reveals that pattern noise is concentrated in a specific case sub-type, focus the next calibration session explicitly on that sub-type. For the security clearance context, that means convening adjudicators to define what constitutes a meaningful foreign contact and what evidence threshold changes the risk assessment. General approval-rate calibration will not reach this.
examples.whyItMatters: Applicants with a single foreign contact received materially different clearance outcomes based on which adjudicator's definition of meaningful contact applied to their case, independently of the contact's actual characteristics.

examples.title: Web App, Infrastructure

planSpec.domain: cybersecurity vulnerability triage

examples.scenario:
You have been using overall analyst agreement rates as your triage quality metric. When two analysts rate the same vulnerability differently, you log the disagreement but do not decompose where it came from. The metric has been stable for two years.

You commission a source decomposition.

Before: you assumed the disagreements were distributed across vulnerability types roughly evenly, with some random variation and some systematic severity differences between analysts. After: you can see the structure. Level noise, some analysts rating all vulnerabilities more severely than others, accounts for twenty-five percent of total inter-analyst spread. Pattern noise, stable analyst-level differences in how web application vulnerabilities are rated compared to network infrastructure vulnerabilities, accounts for forty-nine percent. Occasion noise, within-analyst re-rating of the same vulnerability one month later, accounts for twenty-six percent.

The pattern driver is an exploitability model disagreement. Analysts who believe web application environments have higher base-rate exploitability than network infrastructure give higher severity ratings to web application vulnerabilities relative to peers who hold the reverse belief. Both groups produce the same overall average severity rating across all vulnerability types. The divergence is environment-specific.

"Our team calibration sessions target overall severity averages," the decomposition notes. "The dominant source, forty-nine percent, is a disagreement about attacker behavior models in different environments. We have been calibrating the wrong thing."

Remediation priorities for web application versus infrastructure vulnerabilities still depend on which analyst's exploitability model is applied.
examples.whatToDo: When pattern noise is the dominant component in a triage system, the calibration agenda should address the specific model or assumption that drives the pattern divergence. For vulnerability triage, that means convening analysts to articulate their exploitability assumptions for each environment type and building shared criteria for what constitutes high, medium, and low exploitability in each context.
examples.whyItMatters: Remediation timing for web application vulnerabilities is set by which analyst's exploitability model is applied to that vulnerability class. A vulnerability rated critical by one analyst and high by another receives a different patching timeline, independently of its actual exploitability characteristics.

questions.prompt: Three distinct noise sources are identified in a professional judgment system: level, pattern, and occasion. An organization successfully reduces level noise through calibration. Which statement best describes the effect on total spread?
choices: Total spread decreases only by the proportion attributable to level noise; pattern and occasion noise remain at their original levels.
Total spread decreases substantially because reducing level noise creates conditions that also reduce pattern and occasion noise.
Total spread is unaffected because level noise is typically the smallest of the three components in calibrated organizations, and reducing it produces negligible change.
questions.explanation: Level, pattern, and occasion noise operate independently. Eliminating one component leaves the others unchanged. If level noise is thirty-three percent of total spread, a successful level calibration reduces total spread by thirty-three percent and leaves sixty-seven percent running from the other two sources.

questions.prompt: Within an asylum agency, source decomposition shows: level noise 28%, pattern noise 45%, occasion noise 27%. The agency then invests in a calibration program that successfully equalizes all assessors' overall approval rates. What fraction of total spread remains after this intervention?
choices: Approximately 55 percent remains, from the occasion and level components that the calibration partially addressed.
Approximately 28 percent remains, because the calibration addressed level noise and the other components are smaller.
Approximately 72 percent remains, from pattern and occasion noise, which the calibration did not address.
questions.explanation: Overall approval rate calibration addresses level noise only. Level noise is twenty-eight percent of total spread. Pattern noise (45%) and occasion noise (27%) are unaffected, leaving seventy-two percent of original spread intact after the calibration.

questions.prompt: Within a sports franchise, scout noise decomposition shows pattern noise at 52% of total spread, driven by scouts weighting speed versus football IQ differently on mixed-profile prospects. Which intervention is most directly targeted at the dominant noise source?
choices: Running a calibration session to equalize scouts' overall average prospect ratings across all prospect types.
Convene scouts to develop shared criteria for weighting speed against football IQ on mixed-profile prospects.
Increasing the number of scouts who evaluate each prospect to average out individual variation.
questions.explanation: Pattern noise driven by dimensional weighting differences requires criteria definition at the level of the specific dimension combination that generates divergence. Equalizing overall averages addresses level noise, not pattern noise. Increasing rater count without addressing the divergence source spreads rather than resolves the pattern disagreement.

questions.prompt: A forensic laboratory's proficiency testing shows high examiner accuracy on known-answer cases. A separate noise audit finds that forty-three percent of inter-examiner spread comes from pattern noise in how trace evidence versus biological evidence is rated. What does this combination tell us?
choices: The proficiency results are invalid because the noise audit contradicts them; accurate examiners should not show pattern noise.
Proficiency testing and noise source decomposition measure different things; accuracy on known-answer cases is compatible with substantial pattern noise on ambiguous evidence.
The noise audit is unreliable because examiners who perform well on proficiency tests should not have large pattern components in their disagreement.
questions.explanation: Proficiency testing measures whether examiners can identify correct answers on cases with known ground truth. Noise source decomposition measures whether examiners apply consistent criteria on ambiguous cases where no ground truth exists. An examiner can be highly accurate on proficiency cases while showing substantial pattern noise on significance ratings, because the two tasks are asking different questions.

questions.prompt: A cybersecurity team's noise decomposition shows level noise 25%, pattern noise 49%, occasion noise 26%. The team director decides to run calibration sessions targeting overall severity rating averages. Which assessment of this decision is most accurate?
choices: The intervention is mismatched to the dominant source: overall severity calibration addresses level noise, which accounts for twenty-five percent of spread, while the dominant source at forty-nine percent is pattern noise from exploitability model differences.
The intervention is appropriately targeted because overall severity calibration is the standard first step in any noise reduction program regardless of source decomposition results.

The intervention is correctly matched because occasion noise at twenty-six percent is approximately equal to pattern noise, making average calibration an efficient choice for addressing multiple components simultaneously.
questions.explanation: The decomposition shows pattern noise as the dominant source at forty-nine percent. Overall severity calibration addresses level noise at twenty-five percent. Choosing the lower-value target when the decomposition explicitly identifies a larger one is a mismatch between measurement and intervention.

questions.prompt: An organization's noise decomposition shows level noise at 40%, pattern noise at 35%, occasion noise at 25%. The level component is dominant. What is the appropriate interpretation of this finding for intervention prioritization?
choices: Pattern and occasion noise are negligible and can be ignored once level noise is addressed.
Address level noise first, but design a plan for the pattern and occasion components in parallel, since reducing level noise will not reduce the other two.
The three sources are correlated, so reducing level noise first tends to reduce pattern and occasion noise proportionally as a downstream effect of the calibration program.
questions.explanation: Even when level noise is the dominant source, pattern and occasion noise remain at their original levels after level calibration. They account for sixty percent of total spread and require separate interventions. Addressing the dominant source first is correct prioritization; ignoring the others would leave most of the problem intact.

questions.prompt: A refugee agency runs annual calibration sessions and successfully equalizes assessor approval rates. A new quality director commissions a source decomposition and finds pattern noise still accounts for 45% of total spread. What is the most appropriate next step?
choices: Run a case-type-specific calibration on persecution-type versus documentation weighting, since that pattern-noise driver was not addressed by level calibration.
Run additional cycles of the same level calibration program, since continued practice with overall approval rate alignment will eventually reduce pattern noise as a secondary effect.

Accept the remaining forty-five percent as irreducible variation in asylum assessment, since assessors typically weight persecution type and documentation differently based on the depth of their case experience.
questions.explanation: Level calibration addressed level noise only. Pattern noise concentrated in how assessors weight persecution type versus documentation completeness requires case-type-specific calibration, not overall approval rate alignment. Running more level calibration cycles will not change the pattern-noise component.

questions.prompt: Which feature most clearly distinguishes a judgment system where source decomposition would change the intervention choice from one where it would not?
choices: Total inter-judge spread is above a threshold of thirty percent.
The organization has already run at least one calibration program.
The dominant noise source differs from the source the organization's current interventions address.
questions.explanation: Source decomposition changes the intervention choice only when the dominant source differs from what the current program targets. If calibration is already aimed at the dominant source, decomposition confirms the choice. The value of decomposition is revealing cases where the intervention is aimed at a smaller source while the larger one runs unaddressed.

questions.prompt: An investment committee has successfully calibrated analysts' overall thesis-strength averages over three years. The committee chair argues that this demonstrates the noise problem has been addressed. A noise audit shows pattern noise still accounts for forty-one percent of total spread. Which evaluation of the chair's argument is most accurate?
choices: The chair's argument is correct because overall average calibration is the standard measure of noise reduction.
Partially correct: level noise has been addressed, but pattern noise at forty-one percent remains a separate component needing its own intervention.
The chair's argument is incorrect in all respects because the calibration program has had no measurable effect on total inter-analyst spread.
questions.explanation: The chair is correct that level noise has been addressed and that this represents real progress. The argument is incomplete because pattern noise at forty-one percent of total spread is a separate component that level calibration does not reach. The noise problem has been partially addressed; the dominant component remains.

reviewCards.front: Why does eliminating one noise source fail to reduce the others?
reviewCards.back: Level, pattern, and occasion noise arise from different conditions and respond to different interventions. A calibrated judge has the same overall average as peers but still brings their pattern weighting and their within-day variation. Each source is a separate layer with a separate remedy.

reviewCards.front: What does a source decomposition tell you that total spread does not?
reviewCards.back: Total spread shows how much disagreement exists. Source decomposition shows which component is largest and which intervention will produce the greatest reduction per unit of effort. Without decomposition, intervention choices are made without a map.

reviewCards.front: What is the correct sequence for addressing multi-source noise?
reviewCards.back: Measure first, then intervene. Identify which of level, pattern, and occasion noise is dominant. Target that source with the matched intervention. Then measure again to determine whether the remaining components warrant further action.

reviewCards.front: If a calibration program successfully reduces total spread by 28%, what does that reveal?
reviewCards.back: That the calibrated source accounted for 28% of total spread, and the remaining 72% comes from other sources the program did not reach. Progress on one component does not imply progress on the others.

reviewCards.front: What kind of intervention addresses pattern noise specifically?
reviewCards.back: Case-type-specific criteria definition: specifying what the agreed standard looks like for each major case sub-category, so assessors stop applying private weightings to dimensions the official framework leaves underspecified. Overall average calibration does not reach pattern noise.

implementationPlan.coreSkill: Diagnosing which noise source dominates in a judgment system before choosing an intervention, rather than defaulting to the most visible or most common remedy

ifThenPlans.context: When designing a noise reduction program for a professional judgment system and the dominant source has not been measured
ifThenPlans.plan: Commission a source decomposition before finalizing the intervention design. Estimate level, pattern, and occasion components separately by comparing within-judge across-time variation against between-judge across-case-type variation. The dominant component determines which intervention to prioritize.

ifThenPlans.context: When a calibration program has run for multiple cycles but inter-judge spread remains high
ifThenPlans.plan: Run a source decomposition to determine which component the calibration addressed and which components remain. If pattern or occasion noise accounts for more than forty percent of remaining spread, redesign the intervention to target those sources specifically rather than continuing to refine overall average calibration.

ifThenPlans.context: When evaluating whether a completed noise reduction program succeeded
ifThenPlans.plan: Report the decomposed components before and after, not just overall spread. An intervention that reduced total spread by thirty percent may have fully eliminated the level component while leaving pattern and occasion components at their original levels. Knowing this tells you where the next intervention should focus.

implementationPlan.twentyFourHourChallenge: For one recurring judgment disagreement in your work: identify whether it is always the same person regardless of case type (level), always the same case sub-type (pattern), or the same person at different times on equivalent cases (occasion). Write a sentence naming which source you found. That sentence is the beginning of intervention design.
implementationPlan.weeklyPractice: Once a week, when reviewing disagreements from a recurring judgment process, classify each disagreement by likely source: between-judge general tendency, between-judge case-type-specific tendency, or within-judge temporal variation. After four weeks, check whether one source appears more often than the others. That pattern is your dominant source.

chapters.title: The Mediating Assessments Protocol
chapters.hook: Same judges, same criteria, different order of recording. The spread halved.
chapters.counterintuition: The mediating assessments protocol does not reduce the quality of human judgment; it specifies the sequence in which that judgment operates. Judges in a protocol still exercise full discretion on each dimension. The protocol's noise reduction comes entirely from requiring that discretion to operate before, rather than after, a global impression is formed.
chapters.tryThisNow: For your last evaluation decision: did you have a global sense of the outcome before any dimensional assessment was recorded? If yes, your intermediate scores were made after the conclusion was already present.
chapters.keyTakeaway: The mediating assessments protocol reduces noise by requiring dimensional assessments to be recorded independently before any global judgment is formed. The sequence is not a formality; it is the mechanism.

breakdown.fastRead:
The sentencing commission's holistic evaluation produced an inter-judge variance of fourteen months for matched offense types. Under the mediating assessments protocol, the same judges evaluating the same types of offenses produced a variance of seven months. The judges did not change. The criteria did not change. The order in which assessments were recorded changed.

Recording aggravating factors in writing, before any sentencing number is on the table, prevents those factors from drifting toward a pre-formed conclusion. The protocol requires this discipline at each intermediate step. The final judgment integrates the recorded intermediates rather than a free global intuition.

Holistic evaluation does not feel like contamination. It feels like good judgment operating freely. That feeling is why the contamination is rarely noticed.
breakdown.deepRead:
Two transplant committees assessed the same candidates with different protocols. Under holistic discussion, their listing agreement was 67 percent. Under the mediating assessments protocol, it was 84 percent. That difference has one source: the sequence in which assessments were formed and recorded.

Holistic committee evaluation for transplant listing decisions allows early global impressions to shape all subsequent dimensional assessments before those assessments are recorded. When a transplant committee discusses a candidate's overall suitability before each committee member has independently scored medical eligibility, psychosocial support, and logistical compliance, the candidate who generates a strong positive first impression will see each of those dimensions evaluated generously. The impression forms before the scoring. The scoring then confirms the impression. Research on structured sequential assessment in personnel selection, criminal sentencing, and clinical assessment consistently shows that requiring judges to assess specific intermediate dimensions independently before forming any overall impression reduces inter-judge spread relative to holistic evaluation. The improvement occurs because the structure prevents early global impressions from overwriting dimensional assessments before they are recorded.

The protocol does not trust the judge less. It trusts that any judge, no matter how experienced, will have their dimensional assessments pulled toward whatever global impression formed first. The protocol asks the judge to form no global impression until the dimensions are locked in. That single discipline accounts for most of its noise-reduction effect.

When you skip the protocol and go straight to holistic discussion, you are measuring who had the strongest first impression.
breakdown.fullRead:
The promotion committee had been running on holistic discussion for six years. Four senior executives, reviewing candidates together from the first data point, discussing strengths and weaknesses as they arose. The committee believed it was using sound judgment. The CHRO commissioned a protocol comparison to find out.

Under holistic evaluation, inter-member spread in promotion scores averaged 0.9 points on a 5-point scale. Under the mediating assessments protocol, in which committee members scored leadership style, strategic thinking, and operational performance in writing before any group discussion, spread fell to 0.4 points. The reduction was largest for candidates who generated strong first impressions. Those candidates were exactly the ones most likely to have their dimensional assessments inflated or deflated by the global impression formed in the first few minutes of discussion.

The mediating assessments protocol is not a device for any particular profession. It is what happens when you force the structure that expert intuition is tempted to skip. In criminal sentencing, it separates factor assessment from sentencing anchor. In transplant medicine, it separates dimensional eligibility from overall candidate impression. In loan underwriting, it separates borrower assessment from property quality assessment before those two scores can influence each other. In permit review, it separates environmental impact scoring from technical feasibility scoring. Across all of these contexts, the mechanism is identical: the sequence of independent recordings prevents earlier assessments from contaminating later ones, and prevents any one dimension from becoming a proxy for a global conclusion that has not yet been formally reached.

The effect is largest for high-impression cases because holistic evaluation's contamination is strongest when the global impression is strongest. A candidate who generates immediate enthusiasm will have their strategic thinking score pulled upward not because the evidence warrants it but because the enthusiasm is already in the room. A candidate who generates immediate skepticism will have their operational performance score pulled downward for the same reason. The protocol does not eliminate enthusiasm or skepticism. It prevents those reactions from happening before the evidence is scored.

In practice, the protocol requires three design commitments. The intermediate dimensions must be defined before any specific candidates or cases are reviewed, so that the categories of assessment are fixed before the candidates can shape them. Each dimension must be scored independently in writing before the next is assessed, so that earlier scores cannot be adjusted toward later impressions once both are visible. And the final judgment must integrate the recorded scores through a defined path rather than a free intuition leap from the scores to the conclusion. None of these commitments require judges to exercise less expertise. They require expertise to operate in a disciplined sequence.

The protocol does not require more judgment. It requires the same judgment in a different order, and the order is the change.

memorableLines.text: Holistic evaluation does not feel like contamination. It feels like good judgment operating freely. That feeling is why the contamination is rarely noticed.
memorableLines.why: Names the reason the protocol's value is underestimated: the contamination it prevents is invisible from inside holistic evaluation, which feels like expertise rather than like error.

memorableLines.text: The protocol does not trust the judge less. It trusts that any judge, no matter how experienced, will have their dimensional assessments pulled toward whatever global impression formed first. The protocol asks the judge to form no global impression until the dimensions are locked in. That single discipline accounts for most of its noise-reduction effect.
memorableLines.why: Defuses the expert-resistance objection: the protocol is not a critique of the judge's capability; it is a recognition of how any capable judge's assessments are contaminated by sequence under holistic evaluation.

memorableLines.text: The protocol does not require more judgment. It requires the same judgment in a different order, and the order is the change.
memorableLines.why: The cleanest possible summary of the protocol's mechanism: not added rigor, not additional criteria, just a reordering that prevents the sequence failure holistic evaluation routinely produces.

examples.title: Before the Sentence

planSpec.domain: criminal sentencing with structured factor assessment

examples.scenario:
You are reviewing the commission's protocol comparison study. The cases are matched by offense type, prior record, and jurisdictional guidelines. The judges are the same. The criteria are the same.

Before: under holistic sentencing, judges evaluate all case factors simultaneously and announce a sentence. Inter-judge variance for matched offense types is fourteen months.

After: under the mediating assessments protocol, judges first record their independent assessment of each aggravating factor, then each mitigating factor, then integrate those recorded assessments into a sentencing recommendation. Inter-judge variance for the same matched offense types falls to seven months.

The study isolates the mechanism. Under holistic sentencing, judges reported forming a general sentencing number early in case review and then assessing individual factors in light of that number. Factor assessments that might have pulled the sentence up or down were adjusted toward the pre-formed figure before being recorded. Under the protocol, the factor assessments are recorded before any sentencing number is on the table. They cannot be adjusted toward a conclusion that does not yet exist.

"The judges are not doing less work in the protocol," the study notes. "They are doing more, in a different order, and the order is what prevents each factor assessment from being calibrated to a number the judge has not yet officially reached."
examples.whatToDo: If implementing a structured sentencing or evaluation protocol, require judges to record each intermediate assessment before formulating any final recommendation. The recording must precede the overall conclusion, not follow it. A structured form completed after a global conclusion has been reached does not provide the sequence discipline the protocol requires.
examples.whyItMatters: Defendants in matched cases faced different expected sentences based on which judge's global impression formed first and pulled factor assessments toward it. The protocol reduced that spread by half without changing the criteria or the judges.

examples.title: Two Centers, One Protocol

planSpec.domain: organ transplant candidate evaluation

examples.scenario:
"Our listing agreement rates are at sixty-seven percent for matched candidates," Gertrude said. "Center B is at eighty-four."

Sampson pulled up the protocol description. Center B required each committee member to independently score candidates on three dimensions, medical suitability, psychosocial support, and logistical compliance, before any group discussion began. Scores were recorded in writing. Only after all three scores were submitted for all committee members did the discussion open.

"What is center A's process?"

"Holistic discussion from the start. One member raises an initial impression, others respond, the discussion develops. Everyone scores at the end."

"The problem," Sampson said, "is that scoring at the end means the scores are formed after the impression is fully established. If a candidate generates initial enthusiasm, every subsequent piece of information gets interpreted through that enthusiasm. The medical eligibility question gets a generous read. The psychosocial assessment gets a generous read. By the time anyone scores formally, the scores are just the impression, restated numerically."

"And center B?"

"The protocol asks each dimension before the impression can do that work. When you score medical eligibility without knowing how your colleagues feel about the candidate overall, the score is actually about medical eligibility."

Gertrude looked at the agreement rate again. Seventeen percentage points. Same criteria, different sequence.
examples.whatToDo: When designing transplant listing or any multi-dimensional committee evaluation, require independent dimensional scoring before any group discussion. The scoring form must be completed before the discussion opens, not after. Post-discussion scoring records impressions; pre-discussion scoring records assessments.
examples.whyItMatters: Candidates reviewed by a holistic committee faced listing decisions shaped by which committee member's initial impression was most vocal. Pre-discussion dimensional scoring reduces that dependence.

examples.title: The Spread Below the Spread

planSpec.domain: executive promotion committee

examples.scenario:
The conference table was long enough to seat twelve but held only four. Clementine had arranged the protocol comparison data in two columns: one for each evaluation approach, with the same candidates evaluated under both.

Under holistic committee evaluation, where committee members discussed all candidate factors before individual ratings, inter-member spread in promotion scores averaged 0.9 points on a 5-point scale. Under the mediating assessments protocol, where each member independently scored candidates on leadership style, strategic thinking evidence, and operational performance record before any discussion, spread fell to 0.4 points.

The third table in the packet broke the reduction down by candidate type.

For candidates who generated strong initial reactions, positive or negative, the spread reduction under the protocol was 0.7 points. For candidates who generated moderate initial reactions, the reduction was 0.3 points.

"The protocol's value is largest exactly where we'd assume our judgment is most reliable," Clementine said. "Strong candidate impressions feel like clarity. But the data shows that strong impressions pull dimensional assessments the hardest. When someone seems obviously right for the role, every subsequent piece of evidence gets evaluated through that certainty. The protocol doesn't let that happen."

The committee had always believed its holistic approach produced consistent, well-reasoned evaluations. The protocol study showed it had been producing consistent-seeming evaluations that reflected each member's first impression.
examples.whatToDo: When implementing a promotion evaluation protocol, flag the candidates who generate the strongest immediate committee reactions as the highest-priority cases for pre-discussion dimensional scoring. Those cases have the most to gain from protocol discipline and are most likely to produce inflated or deflated scores under holistic evaluation.
examples.whyItMatters: Promotion outcomes for high-impression candidates were driven by the direction and strength of early committee reactions rather than by dimensional evidence review. The protocol halved the spread for exactly the candidates where that contamination was strongest.

examples.title: Middle of the Pool

planSpec.domain: university scholarship committee

examples.scenario:
The conference room smelled of dry-erase marker and recycled air. Barnard had spread three tables across two pages: one for strong candidates, one for middle-quality candidates, one for weak candidates. Under each table, two rows: holistic discussion agreement rates, then mediating assessments protocol agreement rates.

For strong candidates, agreement was high under both approaches. The evidence was clear, the impressions formed quickly, and the committee converged regardless of method.

For weak candidates, agreement was also high under both approaches. The evidence was clear in the other direction.

For middle-quality candidates, the gap opened.

Under holistic discussion, agreement for middle-quality candidates was 61 percent. Under the mediating assessments protocol, requiring pre-discussion written scores on academic merit, documented financial need, and community impact before any group discussion, agreement rose to 79 percent.

"The middle group is the largest group," Barnard said. "Candidates who are genuinely competitive but not obviously exceptional or obviously unqualified. In holistic discussion, whatever impression forms first in the room determines how their evidence is interpreted. In the protocol, the evidence is scored before the impression can do that."

The eighteen-percentage-point agreement improvement was concentrated entirely in the candidate group that represented the most common case and the most contested award decisions.
examples.whatToDo: When evaluating scholarship or grant applications, implement pre-discussion dimensional scoring especially for the middle-quality range of the applicant pool. Those candidates generate the most variable global impressions and produce the highest disagreement under holistic discussion. The protocol's benefit is largest where the noise is highest.
examples.whyItMatters: A candidate in the middle-quality range had a substantially different expected award outcome depending on which committee member's initial impression shaped the holistic discussion. Structured pre-discussion scoring reduced that dependence.

examples.title: Borrower First

planSpec.domain: commercial lease underwriting

examples.scenario:
Marguerite had initiated the protocol comparison after noticing a pattern in the committee's holistic reviews. Applications with strong borrower presentations, creditworthy financials and confident management teams, tended to receive favorable property and market assessments as well, even in cases where the property's condition or the local market's demand warranted more skepticism. The reverse pattern appeared for weak borrower presentations.

The study confirmed what the pattern suggested.

Under holistic committee review, where members discussed borrower, property, and market factors simultaneously, inter-member spread in credit quality scores averaged 0.8 points on a 10-point scale. Under the mediating assessments protocol, where each member independently scored borrower creditworthiness, property condition, and market demand before any discussion, spread fell to 0.4 points.

The mechanism was visible in the data. Under holistic review, borrower creditworthiness scores and property condition scores for the same application correlated at 0.71. Under the mediating assessments protocol, that correlation fell to 0.34. The borrower-first impression was contaminating the property assessment in holistic review. The protocol broke the spillover.

"A borrower with a compelling presentation should affect the credit quality score," Marguerite noted. "It should not affect the property assessment, which is about the building, not the borrower. Under holistic review, it was affecting both. The protocol let us score the property as a property."
examples.whatToDo: In credit committee review, use the mediating assessments protocol to separately record borrower, property, and market scores before any discussion. After completing the protocol, check whether borrower scores and property scores correlate more than they should given independent evidence. A high correlation under the protocol indicates the dimensions are genuinely related; a high correlation under holistic review indicates contamination.
examples.whyItMatters: Loan applications with strong borrowers received favorable property and market scores that would not have been assigned if the property and market had been assessed before the borrower impression was established. That is a credit risk distortion, not a feature.

examples.title: Assessment Order

planSpec.domain: water discharge permit decision

examples.scenario:
The quality director's question before the pilot study was simple: does the order in which reviewers score permit dimensions affect their final recommendations?

The conventional view in the permit office was no. Reviewers assessed environmental impact, technical feasibility, and monitoring compliance on every permit. The dimensions were the dimensions. The order should not matter.

The pilot study's answer: yes, substantially.

Under holistic review, where reviewers discussed and scored all three dimensions simultaneously, inter-reviewer spread in permit stringency recommendations averaged 0.7 points on a 5-point scale. Under the mediating assessments protocol, where reviewers independently scored environmental impact, then technical feasibility, then monitoring compliance, in that fixed sequence and in writing, before formulating any overall recommendation, spread fell to 0.35 points.

Reviewers who completed the protocol reported that scoring environmental impact first, before reading the technical feasibility section, changed their assessment of the technical section in cases where the environmental impact score was high or low. The technical section no longer had to do the work of anchoring a severity level; the environmental score had already established one.

"The sequence matters because each prior assessment becomes the frame for the next," the quality director noted. "In holistic review, all the frames form simultaneously, which means the loudest one wins. The protocol specifies the frame sequence. That is the whole intervention."
examples.whatToDo: When implementing a permit review protocol, specify the order in which dimensions are scored as well as requiring independent scoring. A protocol that requires independent scoring but leaves the order unspecified produces less noise reduction than one that also defines the sequence. The mechanism requires that each prior assessment constrain the next.
examples.whyItMatters: Permit applicants in the same compliance tier received different stringency recommendations based on how holistic review allowed the most prominent dimension to set the frame for all others. The protocol halved the spread by specifying which dimension sets the frame first.

questions.prompt: Why does requiring independent dimensional assessments before any final judgment reduce inter-judge spread, even when the judges and criteria remain unchanged?
choices: Because judges who complete independent assessments are individually better trained than those who use holistic evaluation.
Because the protocol introduces additional criteria that judges must evaluate, forcing more systematic consideration of each case.
Because recording dimensional assessments before a global impression is formed prevents the global impression from pulling those assessments toward a pre-formed conclusion.
questions.explanation: The protocol's mechanism is sequence, not criteria or training. Judges and criteria are unchanged. What changes is that dimensional assessments are recorded before any global impression is formed, preventing the impression from pulling those assessments toward a conclusion that arrived too early. That contamination prevention is the source of the noise reduction.

questions.prompt: When an executive promotion committee wants to implement a mediating assessments protocol, which design correctly applies the protocol's core principle?
choices: Each committee member ranks all candidates from most to least promising before the meeting, then discusses the rankings.
Each committee member independently scores each candidate on leadership style, strategic thinking, and operational performance before any group discussion begins.
The committee chair assigns a preliminary overall score to each candidate before the meeting to provide an initial reference point for discussion.
questions.explanation: The protocol requires independent scoring of each dimension before any discussion begins. Ranking candidates first creates a global ordering that contaminates dimensional assessments in the same way as holistic discussion. Providing a chair's preliminary overall score creates an anchor, not a protocol. Only independent dimensional scoring before discussion correctly applies the protocol.

questions.prompt: Under holistic evaluation, a transplant committee member who forms a strong positive first impression of a candidate is most likely to do which of the following?
choices: Rate the candidate's medical suitability, psychosocial support, and logistical compliance all higher than they would have under independent dimensional scoring.
Rate the candidate's medical suitability higher but leave psychosocial and logistical assessments unaffected, since those dimensions are independently determined.
Revise the overall impression downward once the dimensional assessments are completed.
questions.explanation: Holistic evaluation allows a positive first impression to pull all subsequent dimensional assessments upward toward the impression, not just the first dimension considered. The contamination is not dimension-specific; it flows from the global impression to every dimensional assessment recorded after it. That is the mechanism the mediating assessments protocol prevents.

questions.prompt: A scholarship committee currently discusses all candidate factors together from the start of deliberation. Which modification is most likely to reduce inter-member spread in award recommendations?
choices: Require each member to independently score academic merit, financial need, and community impact in writing before any group discussion.
Add one more committee member to increase the diversity of perspectives applied to each candidate.
Provide all committee members with a detailed scoring guide that defines each award level but allow continued holistic discussion.
questions.explanation: Independent dimensional scoring before discussion is the protocol modification that breaks the contamination chain. Adding committee members increases the number of global impressions contributing to the discussion without preventing any of them from contaminating dimensional assessments. A detailed scoring guide improves criteria clarity but does not change the sequence; if holistic discussion still precedes scoring, the guide is completed after the impression has formed.
